## Overview

Fix the `functiongemma` tool parser dropping every non-string argument, and make its streamed arguments reassemble into valid JSON. Fixes #63983.

## Claims

- Bare booleans, numbers, `null`, arrays and objects are parsed in streaming and non-streaming, nested containers included.
- Streamed deltas of a multi-argument call concatenate to one JSON object.
- A streamed call still gets closed when its end tag shares a delta with the next call's start tag.
- A streamed call with no arguments sends `{}` instead of an empty string.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_functiongemma_tool_parser.py
pytest tests/entrypoints/tool_parsers/test_functiongemma_tool_parser.py
```

| Parser | parser tests (CPU) | server tests (H200) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main (`eb703fbb3d`) | 25 failed, 17 passed | 3 failed, 4 passed |
| previous head (`fa086599ec`) | 5 failed, 37 passed | 4 failed, 3 passed |
| this PR | 42 passed | 7 passed |

The server tests pin the model output with a `structured_outputs` regex, so they cover serving and parsing rather than what the model decides to call. pre-commit passes on the changed files. Existing Buildkite steps select both test files, but CI has not run on this PR yet.

### End-to-end (vllm serve, real model)

`unsloth/functiongemma-270m-it` (ungated mirror of `google/functiongemma-270m-it`, same `chat_template.jinja`) on one shared H200, through the OpenAI client with `tool_choice="auto"` and `temperature=0`. Streamed `tool_calls` deltas are concatenated per index, as a client would.

```bash
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 vllm serve unsloth/functiongemma-270m-it \
  --tool-call-parser functiongemma --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.04 --enforce-eager --max-num-seqs 4
```

Raw model output for the `set_alarm` request (`/v1/completions`, `skip_special_tokens=false`):

```text
<start_function_call>call:set_alarm{days:[<escape>mon<escape>,<escape>tue<escape>],enabled:true,hour:7,label:<escape>Wake up<escape>}<end_function_call>
```

| Request | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set_alarm` (int, bool, array, string), non-streaming | `{"label": "Wake up"}` | `{"days": ["mon", "tue"], "enabled": true, "hour": 7, "label": "Wake up"}` |
| `set_alarm`, streaming | `{"label": "Wake up"}` | `{"days": ["mon", "tue"], "enabled": true, "hour": 7, "label": "Wake up"}` |
| `get_weather` (two strings), non-streaming | `{"city": "San Francisco", "unit": "celsius"}` | same |
| `get_weather`, streaming | `{"city": "San Francisco"} "unit": "celsius"}` (invalid JSON) | `{"city": "San Francisco", "unit": "celsius"}` |

Review fixes, streaming, same server. The two-call rows pin the output with a regex and set `stream_interval` per request to merge deltas:

| Request | previous head (`fa086599ec`) | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_current_time` (no parameters), real model output | `''` | `{}` |
| Two calls, `stream_interval=4`, delta is `<end_function_call><start_function_call>call:` | `{"city": "Paris"` (invalid JSON) | `{"city": "Paris"}` |
| Two calls, `stream_interval=8`, first call's arguments are in that delta too | `''` | `{"city": "Paris"}` |

Every `stream_interval` from 1 to 6, and 8, gives both calls with valid JSON on this PR.

Screenshots, client script and server logs from the first run (`fa086599ec`): [branch `e2e-evidence-63992`](https://github.com/saifltr/vllm/tree/e2e-evidence-63992/e2e_evidence).

<summary>client</summary>

    "hour": {"type": "integer"}, "enabled": {"type": "boolean"}, "label": {"type": "string"},
    "days": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}}, "required": ["hour", "enabled", "label", "days"]}}}]
PROMPT = "Set an alarm for 7 o'clock labeled Wake up, enabled, on mon and tue."
WEATHER_TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
    "city": {"type": "string"}, "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"]}}, "required": ["city", "unit"]}}}]
WEATHER_PROMPT = "What's the weather in San Francisco in celsius?"

#                                tool_choice="auto", temperature=0, max_tokens=128, stream=stream)

</details>

## Details

The template's `format_argument` macro wraps only strings in `<escape>`, e.g. `enabled:true,hour:7,days:[<escape>mon<escape>],snooze:{minutes:5}`. The old `arg_regex` only matched `key:<escape>...<escape>`, so bare values were dropped. A small recursive parser for that grammar replaces it. With `partial=True` (streaming) it stops at the first incomplete value, so each value is streamed once in its final form. A bare word that is not a JSON literal stays a string.

Streaming diffs are computed by length against `json.dumps(args)`, so the closing brace is held back until the call ends. That left two gaps, both fixed here. When an end tag and the next start tag arrive together, the start branch returned before closing the earlier call, so it never got its brace, or any arguments if they were still unsent. A call with no arguments streamed nothing because the end branch skipped empty arguments. Both paths now go through `_close_tool_call`. Deltas can merge when the client falls behind the engine or `stream_interval` is above 1.

Known limitation: from `stream_interval=10` in these runs, a call's name can share a delta with its end tag, and the name is lost. At 64 the second call is lost too. main behaves the same or worse here, so this is left for a follow-up.

Related PRs:

- #63947 fixes #63906, a separate bug. `<escape>` values keep their current decoding here, so `<escape>123<escape>` is still the integer 123.
- #48705 fixes the brace issue the same way. It is included here because the streaming tests cannot reassemble a multi-argument call without it. Happy to rebase if #48705 lands first.
- #64360 targets the same issue and was opened a day after this PR.

## Details

The template's `format_argument` macro wraps only strings in `<escape>`, e.g. `enabled:true,hour:7,days:[<escape>mon<escape>],snooze:{minutes:5}`. The old `arg_regex` only matched `key:<escape>...<escape>`, so bare values were dropped. A small recursive parser for that grammar replaces it. With `partial=True` (streaming) it stops at the first incomplete value, so each value is streamed once in its final form. A bare word that is not a JSON literal stays a string.

Streaming diffs are computed by length against `json.dumps(args)`, so the closing brace is held back until the call ends. That left two gaps, both fixed here. When an end tag and the next start tag arrive together, the start branch returned before closing the earlier call, so it never got its brace, or any arguments if they were still unsent. A call with no arguments streamed nothing because the end branch skipped empty arguments. Both paths now go through `_close_tool_call`. Deltas can merge when the client falls behind the engine or `stream_interval` is above 1.

Known limitation: from `stream_interval=10` in these runs, a call's name can share a delta with its end tag, and the name is lost. At 64 the second call is lost too. main behaves the same or worse here, so this is left for a follow-up.
